title: Accessible game HUD: colorblind safe and remappable keys
when: The game interface must be readable and playable by more people: colorblind safe colors, remappable controls, scalable text, calmer motion and menus that work with assistive tech.
prompt:
Goal: An options screen and HUD that let players adapt the game instead of fighting it.
Steps:
1. HUD text (score, lives, ammo) lives in HTML over the canvas, updated via textContent only on change; events like "Wave 3" go to a polite aria-live region.
2. Never carry meaning by color alone: pair colors with shapes (enemies triangles, allies circles) and use a deuteranopia safe palette such as #0072b2 and #e69f00.
3. HUD text keeps at least 4.5 to 1 contrast over a semi opaque panel.
4. Remap screen: each action with a "Change" button that waits for the next keydown (Escape cancels), conflicts offer a swap, bindings save to guarded localStorage, plus "Reset to defaults".
5. Options: text size 100 to 150 percent via a CSS variable, shake on or off, flashing off, game speed 75 to 100 percent, toggle instead of hold.
6. Start with the calmer settings when prefers-reduced-motion matches.
7. Menus are real buttons with visible :focus-visible rings, usable by keyboard or d pad.
Quality bar:
- Every function works with one hand on the keyboard.
- Nothing flashes more than 3 times per second.
Pitfalls:
- HUD text painted on the canvas, invisible to screen readers and blurry when scaled.
- Tutorial prompts with hardcoded key names after the player remapped them.
- Announcing the score every frame through aria-live.
Verify:
- [ ] Contrast of HUD text is checked.
- [ ] A remapped jump still works after reload.
- [ ] Reduced motion disables shake.
Output: hud.js, options.js, the HUD and options markup in index.html and style.css.

examples.input: deixar meu jogo acessível para daltônicos e com teclas configuráveis
examples.output: HTML HUD with live events, shape plus color cues, rebinding screen, text size and motion options
